questions.question_text: A person has persistently high blood glucose because pancreatic beta cells produce very little insulin. Which change most directly follows?
questions.option_a: Reduced uptake and storage of glucose in several tissues
questions.option_b: Increased conversion of glycogen to glucose by insulin
questions.option_c: Suppression of all glucagon release by the thyroid
questions.option_d: Immediate loss of calcium from bone due to calcitonin
questions.explanation: Insulin promotes cellular glucose uptake and storage; inadequate secretion can cause hyperglycaemia.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which pancreatic hormone acts in opposition to insulin by raising blood glucose, especially between meals?
questions.explanation: Glucagon from pancreatic alpha cells promotes glucose release, including through glycogen breakdown in the liver.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A prolonged deficiency of iodine may enlarge the thyroid gland because reduced thyroxine weakens which feedback signal?
questions.option_a: Pituitary TSH stimulation of the thyroid
questions.option_b: Insulin release from pancreatic beta cells
questions.option_c: ADH release from the adrenal cortex
questions.explanation: Low thyroid hormone reduces negative feedback, allowing elevated TSH stimulation that can enlarge the thyroid; iodine is needed to synthesise thyroxine.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement about antidiuretic hormone (ADH) is most accurate in humans?
questions.option_a: It is made in the thyroid and increases urine volume
questions.option_b: It is synthesised in the hypothalamus and released into blood from the posterior pituitary
questions.option_c: It is secreted by the adrenal medulla to lower heart rate
questions.option_d: It is produced by pancreatic islets to digest proteins
questions.explanation: ADH is synthesised in hypothalamic neurons and stored and released by the posterior pituitary; it promotes renal water reabsorption.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: After severe dehydration, increased ADH action would normally cause which renal response?
questions.option_a: Less water reabsorbed and a larger volume of dilute urine
questions.option_b: More water reabsorbed and a smaller, more concentrated urine volume
questions.option_d: Loss of glucose reabsorption from every nephron
questions.explanation: ADH increases water permeability in parts of the nephron, conserving water and reducing urine volume.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which pair correctly matches an adrenal region with its principal hormone example?
questions.explanation: The adrenal medulla releases catecholamines including adrenaline; the cortex produces steroid hormones such as cortisol and aldosterone.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: During an acute fight-or-flight response, adrenaline most characteristically helps by
questions.option_a: slowing the heartbeat and constricting the bronchi
questions.option_b: increasing heart activity and mobilising energy reserves
questions.option_c: lowering blood glucose by stimulating insulin release
questions.explanation: Adrenaline prepares the body for rapid action, increasing cardiac activity and making energy substrates more available.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Aldosterone chiefly contributes to regulation of fluid balance by acting on the kidney to increase reabsorption of
questions.option_a: sodium ions, with water following osmotically
questions.option_b: oxygen molecules into red blood cells
questions.option_d: bile salts into the renal tubule
questions.explanation: Aldosterone promotes sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion in the distal nephron; water retention may follow sodium.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which hormone is secreted by the parathyroid glands and generally raises blood calcium concentration?
questions.explanation: Parathyroid hormone raises circulating calcium through actions on bone, kidney and indirectly the intestine.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which thyroid hormone has the most direct opposing effect to parathyroid hormone on blood calcium?
questions.explanation: Calcitonin from thyroid C cells can lower blood calcium, whereas parathyroid hormone raises it; calcitonin's role is less dominant in adult calcium homeostasis.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which hormone most directly stimulates milk synthesis in mammary glands after childbirth?
questions.explanation: Prolactin stimulates milk production; oxytocin causes milk ejection by contracting myoepithelial cells.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Milk is produced normally but the let-down reflex is impaired. Which hormone is most directly implicated?
questions.explanation: Oxytocin triggers milk ejection; prolactin is chiefly responsible for milk synthesis.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which hormone surge is most closely associated with ovulation in a typical human menstrual cycle?
questions.explanation: A mid-cycle LH surge triggers ovulation; FSH and oestrogen also participate in cycle regulation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which hormone is chiefly secreted by the pineal gland and helps synchronise circadian rhythms with the light-dark cycle?
questions.explanation: Pineal melatonin secretion varies with the light-dark cycle and contributes to circadian timing.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The thymus is especially important in childhood because its hormones support maturation of which immune cells?
questions.explanation: The thymus supports maturation of T lymphocytes, central to adaptive cellular immunity.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A child has stunted growth after prolonged deficiency of growth hormone before puberty. Which gland is the principal source of this hormone?
questions.explanation: Growth hormone is secreted by the anterior pituitary; severe deficiency during childhood can impair linear growth.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Excess growth hormone in an adult, after long-bone growth plates have closed, most commonly causes
questions.explanation: Growth hormone excess in adults causes acromegaly, with enlargement of extremities and facial bones; it does not usually increase height after epiphyseal closure.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement best describes a negative feedback loop in endocrine regulation?
questions.option_a: A rise in a hormone's effect can reduce further secretion of the upstream signal
questions.option_b: Every hormone continuously increases its own secretion without limit
questions.option_c: A target gland permanently blocks blood flow to the pituitary
questions.option_d: Hormones act only inside the gland that releases them
questions.explanation: Negative feedback stabilises many endocrine axes: sufficient target-gland hormone suppresses upstream hypothalamic or pituitary signals.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In the hypothalamus-pituitary-thyroid axis, persistently low thyroxine would normally tend to increase secretion of
questions.explanation: Low thyroid hormone weakens negative feedback and tends to increase pituitary TSH stimulation of the thyroid.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The pancreas is called a mixed gland because it
questions.option_a: has only ducts but no hormone-secreting cells
questions.option_b: releases digestive juice through a duct and hormones into the blood
questions.option_c: secretes only hormones into the intestine
questions.explanation: The exocrine pancreas sends digestive enzymes through ducts; endocrine islets release hormones such as insulin and glucagon to blood.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which pancreatic cell-hormone pairing is correct?
questions.explanation: Pancreatic alpha cells secrete glucagon; beta cells secrete insulin.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which feature is characteristic of an endocrine gland rather than an exocrine gland?
questions.option_a: Its secretion is carried by a duct to a body surface
questions.option_b: It releases a hormone into interstitial fluid or blood without a duct
questions.option_c: It secretes digestive enzymes only into the gut lumen
questions.explanation: Endocrine glands are ductless and release hormones into the internal environment, from which they reach target tissues.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A hormone reaches many tissues, but only cells with a matching receptor respond. This selectivity is primarily due to
questions.option_a: the presence of specific receptors in target cells
questions.option_b: the hormone being carried only in arteries
questions.option_c: all cells having identical enzyme sets
questions.option_d: the hormone changing into a nerve impulse in every cell
questions.explanation: Hormone response depends on receptors and intracellular signalling machinery in target cells, not merely blood delivery.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which pair consists of hormones whose secretion can rise during stress and help maintain fuel availability?
questions.explanation: Cortisol and adrenaline are part of stress responses and help mobilise or maintain energy substrates through different mechanisms.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which hormone is produced by the adrenal cortex and helps regulate long-term stress metabolism?
questions.explanation: Cortisol is a glucocorticoid secreted by the adrenal cortex; adrenaline is released by the adrenal medulla.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A hormone deficiency produces low blood calcium and muscle spasms. Deficiency of which gland's hormone is a plausible cause?
questions.explanation: Low parathyroid hormone can cause hypocalcaemia, which may increase neuromuscular excitability and produce tetany.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which sex hormone is chiefly produced by the testes and supports male secondary sexual characteristics?
questions.explanation: Testosterone is the principal androgen produced by Leydig cells of the testes and supports male reproductive development and secondary traits.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: After ovulation, which ovarian structure secretes progesterone that helps maintain the uterine lining in the luteal phase?
questions.explanation: The ruptured follicle becomes the corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone during the luteal phase.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which hormone is essential for normal synthesis of thyroid hormones but is not itself a hormone?
questions.explanation: Iodine is a required raw material in thyroxine and triiodothyronine synthesis; it is a mineral nutrient, not a hormone.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement about the pituitary gland requires the most careful interpretation?
questions.option_a: It is often called the master gland, but hypothalamic signals regulate much of its secretion
questions.option_b: It directly controls every body cell without hormones
questions.option_c: It is an exocrine gland connected to the intestine
questions.option_d: It is the sole source of all hormones in the body
questions.explanation: The pituitary regulates several endocrine glands, but hypothalamic control and feedback from target hormones are central to endocrine regulation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
